heuristic: Delay strong model assumptions; inspect distributions, structure, anomalies and unexpected patterns first.
Identify the observational unit before analysis; distinguish variables, observations and different unit types.
Treat modeling as iterative build-check-validate-understand-compare rather than one-shot fitting.
When the objective is prediction, compare algorithmic models by honest out-of-sample performance rather than privileging one assumed data model.
Keep the first model simple and make the data/serving pipeline trustworthy before adding model complexity.
Explicitly monitor training-serving skew and silent failures.
Check modeling assumptions, overfitting and validation instead of trusting apparent fit.
Time-to-event data with censoring require censor-aware survival representation and evaluation.
Do not start with architecture tuning; inspect data thoroughly first.
Build simple-to-complex and validate one hypothesis/change at a time because neural nets can fail silently.
Define the required visual output and observation unit before selecting the learning architecture.
If multiple non-exclusive defects may coexist, formulate multi-label classification rather than single-label softmax classification.
Always compare a forecasting model against an appropriate naive or seasonal-naive benchmark.
Forecast validation must respect temporal order and forecast horizon.
Select storage/processing architecture by reliability, scalability, maintainability and workload trade-offs, not by technology fashion.
Separate software/pipeline failures from ML-specific distribution shifts and investigate root causes before retraining.
When ground-truth labels are delayed, do not equate input drift with proven performance degradation.
Data augmentation must preserve or correctly transform label semantics; a network can silently train despite an augmentation/label bug.
